primary.title: Goyal calls for trusted India-US supply chains
primary.description: New Delhi: Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal on Thursday called for building resilient and trusted supply chains between India and the US amid prevailing global uncertainties.This helps countries reduce dependence on one geography, securing supplies of critical goods and strengthening India-US economic and strategic ties, the minister said.Addressing the Indo-US Economic Summit here, he said huge potential exists between the two countries to enhance economic cooperation, as the US offers capital, technology, and innovation, while India offers skills, talent, manufacturing strength, and competitiveness.Goyal said he would conclude with five calls to action, using the acronym TRUST to outline his suggestions."T - the first letter. Let us turn our supply chains into resilient and trusted supply chains. 'R', let us raise our talent together with our friendly and partner countries," he said.The minister suggested increasing collaborations between Indian and US universities."I am working with some of them to bring them to India. We'd like to invite all US universities and students to look at India as a part of their program. Because I firmly believe global growth is going to be led from countries in Asia, Africa and Latin America. And time spent by students from the developed world in Indian universities and Indian colleges will help them learn how to deal with us," he added.He said 'S' in the TRUST acronym stands for 'Speak', urging both sides to communicate candidly and openly flag any hurdles or difficulties they face."Let us Speak to each other candidly. Let us flag off the hurdles or the difficulties that anybody faces. So that we can work as your partners to help you in your work. We have different arms of the government which will support you in your work. And help you take your work, take your business to the world," Goyal said.He said the final 'T' stood for 'Track', emphasising the need to monitor outcomes, ensure accountability for performance and urging the IACC to hold both sides accountable.He added that India and the US are two vibrant democracies which shape the global narrative and are important engines for global growth."...an engine always runs on fuel, and that fuel, when it comes to India, is trust. India offers a trusted partnership. India offers our trust, a partner who will stand by you through thick and thin. In every crisis, India is that one partner which never lets its friends down," he added.In a volatile and uncertain world, countries face challenges due to the ongoing wars and the West Asia crisis."In these uncertain times, the world no longer needs just supply chains. They need trusted supply chains. In a trust chain, the partner shares your vision, respects the rule of law, honours contracts and therefore India and the US are natural links who build a chain of trust, a trusted chain. These strong bonds are reflected in our engagement at every level," the minister noted.The minister said the country's exports of goods and services have reached an all-time high of USD 90 billion."That is the India growth story. And that is the story we wish to share with our friends like the United States of America," he added.Meanwhile, speaking at the FICCI event, Goyal said that the country would achieve the USD one trillion exports target during the current fiscal.He added that India must move beyond reducing its dependence on the world and instead make the world dependent on India.He urged FICCI to remake itself as a global chamber at its centenary celebrations.The country, Goyal said, now has the capital, talent, entrepreneurs and banking strength to raise its ambition."Last time I came to your AGM, I spoke about reducing dependence on the world and becoming self-reliant. Today I would like to suggest going one step forward," he said, adding, "We need to make the world dependent upon us. We need to create leverage in India".On trade pacts, he said before 2014, India's free trade agreements covered partners representing USD 10 trillion of global GDP, and the agreements concluded in the past four and a half years have added USD 60 trillion.Negotiations with eight or nine further geographies over the next 18 months would add another USD 15 trillion, giving Indian exporters preferential access to USD 85 trillion, or 76 per cent of global GDP, he added.
